description: Figure 7 presents a grouped bar chart comparing the performance of mBERT and XLM-RoBERTa across nine language families, based on the number of tasks where each model performed better or where performance was the same. The vertical axis, labeled “task count,” ranges from 0 to 40 with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. For each language family, three bars are displayed: light blue for “mBERT better,” dark blue for “XLM-R better,” and light green for “same.” In most families, XLM-R outperforms mBERT, as indicated by taller dark blue bars — notably in IE-Slavic (XLM-R ≈ 39, mBERT ≈ 12, same ≈ 28) and IE-Romance (XLM-R ≈ 13, mBERT ≈ 4, same ≈ 30). mBERT shows a relative advantage only in IE-Germanic (mBERT ≈ 4, XLM-R ≈ 18, same ≈ 22) and IE-Indic (mBERT ≈ 1, XLM-R ≈ 5, same ≈ 4), though XLM-R still leads in absolute count. The “same” category is substantial in several families, especially IE-Romance and IE-Slavic. The legend in the top-right corner clarifies the color coding for the three comparison outcomes.
